stem:
Meena's school garden in Jaipur has patches of different soils. After watering, she notices water sinking into the ground at different speeds.

In which material will water seep through fastest?

options.text: Clay, because its particles are the finest and its surface looks smooth.
Gravel, because the spaces between its particles are wide and well connected.
Sand, because it is lighter in colour than the other materials.
Clay, because it holds the greatest total amount of water.

teacher.key_rationale: Water seeps fastest through materials with wide, open, connected spaces between particles. Gravel has the widest connected pores, so it lets water pass fastest; sand is slower and clay slowest. Option A is the trap for students who assume finer, smoother particles allow faster seepage.
